scope: Review pi-auth.js and pi-native.js for Pi 0.80 CredentialStore compatibility, OAuth shape preservation, refresh persistence, legacy api-key fallback, and edge cases.
result_json: {"angle":"OAuth credential-store compatibility","summary":"OAuth shape preservation, delegated refresh persistence, and legacy api-key fallback are implemented and covered by focused tests, but credential-store read failures from the Pi auth file are swallowed as missing credentials instead of surfacing as Pi 0.80 auth/storage failures.","ready":false,"findings":[{"severity":"medium","file":"packages/agent-runtime/src/ai/providers/pi-native.js","line":104,"evidence":"`readCredential` calls `resolvePiApiKey.readCredential(provider)` but catches any thrown error, pushes `pi_auth_failed`, and returns `undefined` at lines 100-110. The injected resolver's `readCredential` reads the auth file at `packages/agent-runtime/src/pi-auth.js:61`, and `readAuthFile` throws on invalid JSON at lines 138-146. Pi 0.80's installed `CredentialStore` contract says store methods reject on storage failure, and `resolveProviderAuth` wraps read rejections as `ModelsError(\"auth\", \"Credential store read failed...\")`. A temp-file repro with `{not-json` returned no credential plus a warning instead of rejecting: `{\"warnings\":[{\"warning_kind\":\"pi_auth_failed\",\"provider\":\"openai-codex\",\"message\":\"Unable to parse Pi auth file ...\"}]}`.","impact":"A corrupt or unreadable Pi auth store is converted into a missing credential. For OAuth-only providers such as `openai-codex`, this can still lead to the misleading no-credential/no-API-key path instead of a precise credential-store auth failure; for API-key-capable providers it can silently fall through to ambient env auth even though Pi 0.80 treats stored credential failures as auth errors.","recommendation":"Do not swallow errors from the enhanced credential-store `readCredential` path. Let storage/read failures reject so Pi `Models` wraps them as auth failures, while preserving the legacy soft-fallback behavior only for the old string `resolvePiApiKey(provider)` callback path. Add a regression test where `resolver.readCredential` throws and `store.read(provider)` rejects rather than returning `undefined`.","validation":"Repro: `node --input-type=module` importing `createPiOAuthApiKeyResolver` and `createDynamicCredentialStore`, writing `{not-json` to a temp auth file, then `await store.read('openai-codex')`; current behavior returns undefined with a `pi_auth_failed` warning. Existing checks run: `pnpm --filter @mono-agent/agent-runtime test -- src/__tests__/ai/pi-native.test.js src/__tests__/pi-auth.test.js --runInBand` passed; `pnpm --filter @mono-agent/agent-runtime run build` passed."}],"false_positives_considered":["OAuth credential shape preservation is covered: `pi-native.js` uses `resolvePiApiKey.readCredential` and accepts `{ type: \"oauth\", ... }`; `pi-native.test.js:102-123` verifies the legacy api-key resolver is not called for OAuth store reads.","OAuth refresh persistence is covered: `pi-native.js:137-138` delegates `modify` to `resolvePiApiKey.modifyCredential`, and `pi-auth.js:72-82` serializes read-modify-write updates; tests at `pi-native.test.js:125-156` and `pi-auth.test.js:81-114` validate persistence and shape.","Legacy API-key fallback still works: without credential-store methods, `pi-native.js:113-114` wraps the string callback result as `{ type: \"api_key\", key }`, and `pi-native.test.js:97-100` covers that path.","The outdated public JSDoc/type shape for `createPiOAuthApiKeyResolver` hides the new methods in generated declarations, but it does not break the live host path because the returned function still carries the methods at runtime; treat it as documentation/type debt unless this PR is expected to publish the enhanced resolver contract."],"recommended_parent_action":"Fix the credential-store read error semantics before merging, then rerun the focused agent-runtime auth tests and package build. The rest of the OAuth preservation/refresh behavior in this scope looks correct."}

scope: Review ai/runtime/router.js plus ai/failure.js/result-builder.js for correct terminal auth behavior, retryable availability fallback, exhaustion labeling, and artifact failover history.
Review observability failure-kind and artifact-audit changes for provider_auth compatibility, operator-facing messaging, known-kind histograms, and persisted summary contract risks.
result_json: {"angle":"Observability taxonomy","summary":"Focused plan tests pass and the observability taxonomy/schema now knows provider_auth, but the router still preserves an auth-text provider_unavailable result as provider_unavailable, so one compatibility path can still persist/count auth failures as availability.","ready":false,"findings":[{"severity":"medium","file":"packages/agent-runtime/src/ai/runtime/router.js","line":184,"evidence":"For terminal non-retryable failures the router returns `{ ...result, failoverHistory }` unchanged. The focused router test at packages/agent-runtime/src/__tests__/ai/router.test.js:136-153 constructs `error: \"401 invalid api key — authentication failed\"` with `failureKind: \"provider_unavailable\"` and asserts the final `result.failureKind` remains `provider_unavailable`, even though packages/agent-runtime/src/ai/failure.js:209 classifies auth text as `provider_auth`.","impact":"Any provider/runtime result that still enters the router as `provider_unavailable` with missing/invalid credential text will be persisted as provider availability, counted in the provider_unavailable histogram, and shown with provider-availability operator guidance rather than credential repair guidance. This satisfies terminal/no-exhaustion behavior but not the stated taxonomy requirement to classify invalid credentials as `provider_auth`.","recommendation":"Normalize auth-like terminal provider results before returning them from the router, or require all adapters to emit `provider_auth` before the router sees them. Update the invalid-api-key router test to expect `provider_auth` and keep the existing no-fallback assertion.","validation":"After updating the router test expectation to `provider_auth`, run `pnpm --filter @mono-agent/agent-runtime test -- src/__tests__/ai/router.test.js src/__tests__/ai/failure.test.js --runInBand`; rerun `pnpm --filter @mono-agent/observability test -- src/__tests__/failure-kinds.test.ts src/__tests__/artifact-audit.test.ts --runInBand` to confirm the persisted taxonomy/audit surface still passes."}],"false_positives_considered":["I did not treat adding `provider_auth` to `failureKindHistogram` as a breaking persisted-summary change: `failureKind` remains an open string on `RunSummary`, and `KnownArtifactFailureKind` plus `KNOWN_ARTIFACT_FAILURE_KINDS` were updated together.","I did not flag the artifact-audit test's `provider_auth: 0` as a defect. The audit code seeds and counts from the shared known-kind list, so a positive fixture would improve coverage but is not required to prove the key is recognized.","The plan's focused tests passed in this workspace: agent-runtime reported 44 test files / 569 tests passed, and observability reported 16 test files / 161 tests passed. That confirms the current suite is green but also confirms the stale router expectation is still encoded."],"recommended_parent_action":"Request a small follow-up before merging: normalize auth-like `provider_unavailable` terminal results to `provider_auth` in the router/adapters and update the router regression test. The observability display taxonomy and artifact-audit known-kind additions otherwise look consistent."}

scope: Review added/updated tests and verification claims for real behavior coverage, red-green validity, missing negative cases, and whether live verification proves the original personal-agent issue.
result_json: {"angle":"Tests and verification coverage","summary":"Focused runtime and observability suites pass, and the new tests are red-green for OAuth credential preservation, credential-store refresh writes, and router terminal handling. The remaining gap is that no test exercises the Pi-native result-builder path that turns an actual Pi auth error into the artifact failureKind; the documented live success run also does not prove the broken-auth artifact path.","ready":false,"findings":[{"severity":"medium","file":"packages/agent-runtime/src/ai/providers/pi-native/result-builder.js","line":171,"evidence":"The changed Pi-native result assembly sets failureKind by calling failureKindForPiError at lines 171-172 (and the outer catch does the same at line 226), but `rg -n \"failureKindForPiError|provider_auth|No API key|OAuth refresh\" packages/agent-runtime/src/__tests__ packages/agent-runtime/src/ai/providers/pi-native` shows no test importing/calling failureKindForPiError or buildErrorResult/buildStreamFinalResult for an auth error. The added tests cover classifyFailure for `No API key...` and a router result where `failureKind: \"provider_auth\"` is already supplied, so a regression in this Pi-native artifact-mapping path would still be missed. The plan's live claim is a successful run on pi:openai-codex, which proves repaired OAuth works but not that a missing/invalid/refresh-failed Pi credential records provider_auth instead of provider_unavailable/provider_unavailable_exhausted.","impact":"The original personal-agent issue had two visible symptoms: OAuth credential shape loss and misleading provider_unavailable_exhausted artifacts. The tests strongly cover the credential-shape fix, but they do not directly prove the artifact classification part on the actual Pi-native result path. A future regression could reintroduce misleading auth-failure artifacts while the current focused tests still pass.","recommendation":"Add a focused Pi-native result-builder regression, preferably asserting `failureKindForPiError(\"No API key for provider: openai-codex\", {}, {}) === \"provider_auth\"` and that `buildErrorResult` or the stream-final result builder records `failureKind: \"provider_auth\"` for the same error. If live verification is kept as release evidence, add a negative smoke using a temporary missing/invalid openai-codex credential store and verify the artifact failureKind is provider_auth.","validation":"Ran `pnpm --filter @mono-agent/agent-runtime test -- src/__tests__/ai/pi-native.test.js src/__tests__/pi-auth.test.js src/__tests__/ai/failure.test.js src/__tests__/ai/router.test.js --runInBand` (passed: 44 files, 569 tests) and `pnpm --filter @mono-agent/observability test -- src/__tests__/failure-kinds.test.ts src/__tests__/artifact-audit.test.ts --runInBand` (passed: 16 files, 161 tests); also ran `rg -n \"failureKindForPiError|provider_auth|No API key|OAuth refresh\" packages/agent-runtime/src/__tests__ packages/agent-runtime/src/ai/providers/pi-native` to confirm the missing direct result-builder coverage."}],"false_positives_considered":["The new credential-store tests are meaningful red-green tests: old code would call the legacy resolver and fail to preserve OAuth objects, while the new tests assert read/modify/delete behavior on the resolver-backed store.","The router test is valid for router behavior because the router should trust a provider-supplied provider_auth failureKind and stop fallback; it just does not prove the Pi-native provider supplies that kind from auth error text.","The successful personal-agent run and OK_OAUTH_STORE claim are useful live evidence for OAuth credential preservation, but they are positive-path checks and cannot prove the negative broken-auth artifact classification path."],"recommended_parent_action":"Request one additional Pi-native result-builder/provider_auth regression, then rerun the same focused agent-runtime and observability suites. The live success evidence can stand for credential preservation, but add a negative auth-artifact smoke if the parent wants live proof of the original misleading-artifact symptom."}

scope: Review public host/runtime API compatibility around resolvePiApiKey, added function properties, JSDoc/type contract drift, package boundaries, and downstream host impact.
result_json: {"angle":"Backward compatibility and public API","summary":"Runtime compatibility for legacy string resolvers is preserved, and the OAuth credential-store path is additive. One public API contract drift remains: the resolver factory JSDoc still advertises a plain string-only callback even though the returned function now carries credential-store methods used by the fix, so generated declarations and downstream TypeScript/docs will not expose the new contract.","ready":false,"findings":[{"severity":"medium","file":"packages/agent-runtime/src/pi-auth.js","line":11,"evidence":"The factory JSDoc still declares `@returns {(provider: string) => Promise<string|undefined>}` while the implementation attaches public credential-store methods on the returned function at lines 57, 65, and 85. The currently generated public declaration mirrors the narrow return type in `packages/agent-runtime/types/pi-auth.d.ts:4-8`, so TypeScript consumers of `createPiOAuthApiKeyResolver()` cannot see `.readCredential`, `.modifyCredential`, or `.deleteCredential`, and the host `resolvePiApiKey` contract remains documented as string-only.","impact":"The runtime fix works for JavaScript and for passing the factory result into the runtime, but the newly added function-property API is invisible to downstream TypeScript hosts and custom resolver authors. That makes the public package contract drift from the behavior required for Pi 0.80 OAuth refresh persistence, increasing the chance that host code reimplements only the legacy string resolver and silently regresses OAuth credential preservation.","recommendation":"Introduce an explicit exported JSDoc typedef for the credential shape and resolver intersection, e.g. a callable `PiApiKeyResolver` with optional `readCredential`, `modifyCredential`, and `deleteCredential` methods; update the factory return annotation and `AgentRuntimeHostOptions.resolvePiApiKey` docs/types to use it; regenerate declarations with the package type build.","validation":"rg -n \"@returns \\{\\(provider: string\\)|readCredential|modifyCredential|deleteCredential|resolvePiApiKey\" packages/agent-runtime/src/pi-auth.js packages/agent-runtime/types/pi-auth.d.ts packages/agent-runtime/src/ai/types.js"}],"false_positives_considered":["Legacy `(provider) => Promise<string|undefined>` resolvers remain supported: `packages/agent-runtime/src/ai/providers/pi-native.js:80-84` calls the function when no credential-store method exists, and `:113-114` wraps a returned string as `{ type: \"api_key\", key }`.","The new resolver methods are optional, not required for existing hosts: `readCredential`, `modifyCredential`, and `deleteCredential` are all guarded with `typeof ... === \"function\"` before use in `packages/agent-runtime/src/ai/providers/pi-native.js:100`, `:137`, and `:152`.","Adding `provider_auth` itself appears backward-compatible because the failure taxonomy is already open in `packages/agent-runtime/src/ai/failure.js:15-20`, and observability lists were extended in the scoped files.","No package-boundary violation was found in the scoped implementation: the new auth classifier import stays within `@mono-agent/agent-runtime`, and observability changes remain in `@mono-agent/observability`."],"recommended_parent_action":"Do not merge as-is; update the public JSDoc/generated declaration contract for `resolvePiApiKey` and rerun the agent-runtime type build plus the focused Pi auth/provider tests before landing."}

scope: Review auth file handling, credential secrecy, clone/write semantics, locking/serialization, race conditions, and whether logs/artifacts could expose secrets.
result_json: {"angle":"Security and concurrency","summary":"Found one concurrency defect in the auth-file write path: refresh writes are serialized per provider even though each write rewrites the whole auth JSON file, so concurrent refreshes for different providers can lose one update. I did not find evidence that the changed code directly logs credential values.","ready":false,"findings":[{"severity":"medium","file":"packages/agent-runtime/src/pi-auth.js","line":72,"evidence":"`modifyCredential` queues by `provider` via `enqueue(provider, ...)` at line 72, but it reads the whole auth object and rewrites the whole file at lines 73-78, and `writeAuthFile` renames a complete JSON file at lines 158-164. I reproduced the race with one resolver and two concurrent `modifyCredential` calls for providers `a` and `b`; the final file contained `a.access = a-new` but `b.access = b-old`, proving one refresh update was dropped.","impact":"Concurrent OAuth refreshes for different providers in the same auth file can silently resurrect stale credentials. This can cause later provider_auth failures even though the refresh callback reported success, and it can also drop a concurrent delete or update if a direct legacy resolver write interleaves with store writes.","recommendation":"Serialize auth-file read-modify-write operations at the auth-file level, not the provider level, and route all write paths through the same lock, including the legacy `resolvePiOAuthApiKey` refresh path. Add regression coverage for concurrent updates to two different providers and, ideally, two resolver instances pointing at the same auth path.","validation":"Reproduce with: `node --input-type=module <<'NODE' ... import { createPiOAuthApiKeyResolver } from './packages/agent-runtime/src/pi-auth.js'; create temp auth with providers a/b; run Promise.all([resolver.modifyCredential('a', async c => { await barrier; return { ...c, access: 'a-new' }; }), resolver.modifyCredential('b', async c => { await barrier; return { ...c, access: 'b-new' }; })]); print auth.json ... NODE`; expected after fix: both a-new and b-new are present. Focused regression command: `pnpm --filter @mono-agent/agent-runtime test -- src/__tests__/pi-auth.test.js --runInBand`."}],"false_positives_considered":["The existing same-provider concurrent refresh test at `packages/agent-runtime/src/__tests__/pi-auth.test.js:116` is not sufficient evidence of safety because it only exercises one provider and writes the same new credential value every time.","The shallow clone helper in `createPiOAuthApiKeyResolver` appears acceptable for the current flat Pi OAuth credential shape; I did not file it as a defect without evidence of nested mutable credential fields.","The temp-file-plus-rename path keeps the auth file mode at 0600 and avoids torn writes in normal operation; the filed issue is lost updates from insufficient serialization granularity, not world-readable credential output.","`runtimeWarnings` still store auth error messages, but I did not find a changed path that writes actual access or refresh token values into logs or artifacts."],"recommended_parent_action":"Request a fix before merge: replace the provider-scoped queue with auth-path/file-scoped serialization for every auth file write path, then add the multi-provider concurrent refresh regression and rerun the focused agent-runtime auth tests."}
